paragraphs: Children in care in Staffordshire are looked after by the county council's own service, Foster with Staffordshire, and by the independent agencies listed on this page. In January 2026 the council said it needed 60 more foster families during the year, and that people from all walks of life can and do foster with it.

Staffordshire is a large county and the council says it needs carers in every part of it. Its fostering pages describe four areas, Burton, Newcastle, Staffordshire Moorlands and Lichfield, and people living just outside the county may still be able to apply if they are within a 30-minute commute of a Staffordshire town. Applicants and approved carers use the Fostering Village, the council's online space for starting an application, following the steps to approval and keeping up with paperwork.

Staffordshire's 2026-27 Payment for Skills scheme pays a weekly allowance for each child, from £178.18 for a child under two to £267.50 for a 16 or 17 year old. Carers at Levels 2 to 4 receive a weekly skills fee on top, which rises with the child's age and the carer's level, and carers with relevant childcare experience can be considered to start at Level 3. Every child also attracts birthday, festival and summer holiday grants. Our Staffordshire allowance page has the full tables.

Agencies set their own fees and support, so it is worth speaking to the council and two or three of the agencies below, and asking each about training, local support groups and out-of-hours help, before you decide.

sources.title: Foster family urges others to make fostering their new year's resolution (Staffordshire County Council)
